about: A batch is judged before anything of it lands. The pass before it takes the batch, signed as accept will sign it, and renders the tree with its lines in; accept folds the same signed lines over that tree, judges every take and runs the gates once on that fold, and lands only when all of it holds.
A batch refused leaves nothing of itself: no line, no take marked open. What the instrument keeps of its own folds while judging is its memory, not the batch.
